paper: The First Answer Is Not Enough: An Architecture for AI-Assisted Deliberation Before Decision
software_examined: WebChess 2.2.0 release candidate at 7a3749cf7f2c4e4c5ebfeb9b9aa870a11843f3a2 (committed; not tagged; not deployment proof)
fact_boundary: No figure reports effectiveness data. Measured figures are limited to current perft and pinned engine-arena regression results.

figures.title: The first frame should not become a monopoly
figures.alt_text: A forked flow contrasts a one-pass path from ambiguous question to first frame and fluent answer with the Arachne Method path through structured plurality, conflict, examination, and qualified action.
figures.caption: The Arachne Method delays premature closure by separating problem construction from selection, examination, qualification, and consequence. This is the architecture's thesis, not a measured effectiveness claim.

figures.title: Eight authorities, seven visible stops, one Answer artifact
figures.alt_text: Two horizontal rails compare the eight formal Arachne authorities with the seven player-facing lifecycle stops, showing Gate and Retry as internal authorities and Answer as a generated artifact.
figures.caption: The architecture counts Anansi, Chess, Portia, Gate, Retry, Charlotte, Wilbur, and the Web. The interface instead shows Anansi, Chess, Portia, Answer, Charlotte, Wilbur, and Web; Answer is not a ninth authority.

figures.title: Anansi's 8 × 8 field: sixty-four bounded facets
figures.alt_text: An eight-by-eight matrix crosses Purpose, People, Resources, Timing, Risks, Values, Evidence, and Possibilities with Begin, Receive, Clarify, Connect, Challenge, Adapt, Consolidate, and Release.
figures.caption: Every facet occupies one practical-dimension by change-movement coordinate. Structural coverage constrains generation but does not prove completeness or correctness.

figures.title: One seed, three independent deterministic shuffles
figures.alt_text: A saved seed fans into separate facet, lens, and board permutations before producing the initial semantic board.
figures.caption: The cast independently permutes facets, I Ching-inspired lenses, and completed pairs onto board locations. It is reproducible recombination, not semantic inference or evidence.

figures.title: The board as P₈ □ C₈: bounded rings, cyclic sectors
figures.alt_text: An eight-ring radial board is paired with the notation P8 Cartesian-product C8, explaining bounded ring positions, cyclic sector positions, and sixty-four cells.
figures.caption: WebChess coordinates form eight bounded ring positions crossed with eight wrapping sector positions. The notation describes cell topology; piece rules still define legal movement.

figures.title: Initial position and the two nonmoral polarities
figures.alt_text: A radial chess board shows Black back pieces and pawns at the center moving outward and White pieces and pawns at the edge moving inward.
figures.caption: Black represents inside-out intent from rings zero and one. White represents outside-in evidence from rings seven and six and moves first. The colors are directional, not moral.

figures.title: Six movement roles, six metaphors of attention
figures.alt_text: Six cards map King, Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight, and Pawn to core purpose, agency, structure, perspective, reframing, and practice, while summarizing their implemented movement.
figures.caption: Piece metaphors translate chess roles into modes of attention. They organize inquiry without assigning truth or stakeholder worth.

figures.title: Attention is a display score—not an epistemology
figures.alt_text: The implemented capture-attention equation appears above four separated scales: piece value, engine evaluation, capture attention, and evidence or human value.
figures.caption: The capture score combines a constant, piece values, and a middle-ring meeting bonus. It must not be promoted into probability, evidence quality, moral importance, or decision benefit.

figures.title: Engine V2: a principal-variation search web
figures.alt_text: A branching search tree highlights one principal variation and defines PVS, TT, SEE, and quiescence alongside the deterministic node budget.
figures.caption: Engine V2 uses iterative principal-variation alpha-beta search, aspiration windows, a transposition table, quiescence, static exchange evaluation, and a seeded root tie-break. It has no semantic access.

figures.title: Terminal precedence: the decisive condition wins first
figures.alt_text: A five-step vertical decision order checks King capture, mutual immobility, one hundred quiet plies, two hundred fifty-six completed plies, then continuation or forced pass.
figures.caption: A direct King capture is evaluated before draw boundaries. This makes a capture on ply 256 a win rather than a move-limit draw.

figures.title: Authoritative replay: derive state, never trust it
figures.alt_text: A small browser command passes through load, canonical rebuild, replay, resolution, and atomic compare-and-swap commit stages.
figures.caption: The browser proposes only a piece, destination, and expected revision. The server reconstructs and validates the authoritative game before committing derived events.

figures.title: Portia hunts the prompt before an Answer exists
figures.alt_text: Thirteen named adversarial attacks orbit a Portia center, with preserved, wounded, consumed, and unresolved dispositions below.
figures.caption: Every terminal candidate is tested exactly once against thirteen versioned attack types. Portia reviews the exact forthcoming Answer prompt before generation.

figures.title: The Gate is a conjunction, not an oracle
figures.alt_text: Seven requirement cards converge on an AND gate that authorizes Answer only when every hard floor passes.
figures.caption: webchess-gate-v4 requires Portia permission, minimum usable and independent candidates, required coverage, explicit tension, contradiction safety, and qualification integrity.

figures.title: Retry is a finite tree, not an infinite reroll
figures.alt_text: A failed Gate can spend at most two root-wide same-field replay allowances and one field-regeneration allowance, in policy-selected order, before an explicit insufficient-basis stop.
figures.caption: Two root-wide replay children plus one regenerated-field child cap a genealogy at four games. The policy chooses their order; duplicate fingerprints favor regeneration.

figures.title: Answer → Charlotte → durable Wilbur
figures.alt_text: Four cards flow from approved prompt to stored Answer, Charlotte qualification with exactly three suggestions, and a durable Wilbur mutation boundary with once-only rate admission, lifetime capacity reservation, atomic settlement, and exact replay.
figures.caption: Gate-approved Answer is stored, then Charlotte qualifies it. Every Wilbur create, update, or observation is owner-, idempotency-key-, and digest-bound; admission uses database time, and the artifact, lifecycle event, and ledger result settle atomically. Wilbur executes and independently verifies neither.

figures.title: The Web remembers—including failure
figures.alt_text: A circular provenance graph connects question, facets, cast, event log, terminal ecology, Portia, Gate, Answer, Charlotte, Wilbur action, observations, and the durable mutation ledger around a central Web.
figures.caption: The implemented Web is within-case provenance with owner scope, versions, digests, append-only lifecycle events, and terminal Wilbur mutation outcomes. Consented cross-case learning is not implemented.

figures.title: Three audited runtime boundaries
figures.alt_text: Three columns distinguish the tagged v2.1.0 OpenClaw release line, the committed but undeployed hosted-service architecture, and the working local source-checkout topology in the committed WebChess 2.2.0 candidate.
figures.caption: The local checkout now supports either a signed no-Clerk session or a complete Clerk development-key pair, validates its loopback PostgreSQL boundary, applies exact-prefix canonical migrations only under launcher authority, and waits for readiness before opening the browser. The candidate is not tagged, and no hosted deployment is claimed.

figures.title: Evidence labels prevent architectural time travel
figures.alt_text: A six-level tapered ledger separates the tagged v2.1.0 release, committed WebChess 2.2.0 candidate at 7a3749c, absent deployment proof, unit and PostgreSQL tests, combined coverage, and browser, accessibility, and audit gates.
figures.caption: The immutable candidate passed 82 unit files with 1,177 tests, 9 PostgreSQL files with 61 tests, a combined 91-file/1,238-test coverage run at 84.66% statements, 80.76% branches, 88.51% functions, and 85.78% lines, plus 145 Playwright tests, 6 expected Clerk skips, 32 accessibility checks, and zero dependency-audit findings. These overlapping gates are not additive and are not deployment or effectiveness proof.

figures.title: Perft: measured rule-space fingerprints
figures.alt_text: Horizontal bars show exact perft leaf counts for the initial position, a bishop crossing the sector seam, and a rook circling the seam at depths one and two.
figures.caption: The audit reproduced canonical perft counts: initial 20 and 400; bishop seam 13 and 65; rook seam 12 and 60. These validate bounded rule behavior, not playing strength.

figures.title: Arena: a bounded strength-regression result
figures.alt_text: A paired-color arena card reports Engine V2 depth three against legacy-greedy-v1 across three seeded openings, with six win tokens and a six-zero-zero record.
figures.caption: The current deterministic arena produced W-D-L 6-0-0 over six paired-color legs. This is regression evidence against a pinned baseline, not Elo or evidence of reasoning benefit.

figures.title: How the architecture should be tested
figures.alt_text: Five experimental arms—direct answer, self-refine, capture trail, full lifecycle, and ablations—flow into matched tasks and blinded evaluation metrics.
figures.caption: A credible evaluation compares the full lifecycle with strong baselines and ablations while measuring quality, calibration, downstream learning, cost, latency, harms, and refusal.

figures.title: Eight metaphors—and the point where each must break
figures.alt_text: Eight cards around a web pair each Arachne authority with its functional metaphor and a warning against overextending the analogy.
figures.caption: Metaphors make authority boundaries memorable. Typed contracts, failure states, provenance, and evaluation—not mythological resonance—make the method accountable.

figures.title: Formal model: a provenance-preserving flow
figures.alt_text: Eleven equation cards trace the field, cast, game, survivors, exact prompt package, Portia, Gate, the distinct Answer artifact, Charlotte, the human-authored Wilbur record, and the within-case Web.
figures.caption: The notation matches the paper's formal chain and keeps Prompt Package, Answer, Charlotte qualification, Wilbur's player-authored report, and the provenance Web distinct. The equations imply neither autonomous execution, independent verification, nor a proven world-state transition; Figure 8 separately shows the implemented Wilbur durability controls.

figures.title: The durable Web: twenty physical tables
figures.alt_text: Five linked panels enumerate the migration ledger and all nineteen application tables across governance, play and limits, lifecycle, human records and mutation claims, and model research boundaries.
figures.caption: Thirteen ordered migrations define nineteen application tables plus the migration ledger, twenty physical tables total. The release contract also verifies eight critical unique or primary-key indexes, two exact guarded trigger/function pairs, eighteen critical constraints, and five defaults.

figures.title: Two short transactions around remote inference
figures.alt_text: An authenticated intent passes through a reservation transaction, bounded provider call, settlement transaction, and durable response, with four interruption outcomes below.
figures.caption: WebChess commits before inference and settles afterward. Ambiguous provider-started work becomes indeterminate; there is no silent replay. This is application recovery, not backup.

figures.title: Deletion boundary: verified, ordered, atomic
figures.alt_text: Two independent entries are shown: self-deletion branches to a 409 no-loss stop while provider work is in progress or to content cleanup and a suspended identity marker; the signed user-deleted webhook enters the force path directly.
figures.caption: Both paths use the foreign-key-safe game-first order under the shared lock. On the force path, game cascades occur first; under that same lock, the lifetime HMAC barrier is then established before request-ledger and raw-identity deletion, and all changes commit atomically. Mature artifacts, force, retries, and refunds are integration-tested.
